utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when we left off on Friday, you were discussing arrival -- your arrival in Grabovica and how people were relaxed and fishing and swimming and having a decent time. And then I asked you: Did Celo and Caco's unit arrive shortly after your units arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, when he asked that, I objected. Because, Your Honour, it's the blurring of those two units together which has been objected to all along, and I maintain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he objected and you alloyed me to ask the question first as a general question and then to get into specifics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's the same -- the exact question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you could ask some -- you know, even more general question, in that what are the units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And later on step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was planning to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So what units arrived in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Independent, Celo's people. Caco's men were not in Grabovica. They were accommodated somewhere else. And a unit call Cedeni Vukovi, Cedo's Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after Cedo's unit arrived, did the atmosphere in Grabovica change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us how it changed, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they arrived at Grabovica, after a certain amount of time, they started shooting, taking civilians away. They were under the influence of drugs and alcohol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did the change occur immediately upon their arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did this change occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what could you hear beginning in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shouting, shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what -- what did you think when you heard this shouting and shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were just having fun, a good time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to the early evening. Do you know a -- another soldier with the nickname of Tajso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us, Witness E, whether you and Tajso did anything in the evening or in the early evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please tell the Court what you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the house. And then we went to pick some tomatoes and paprika, or peppers. We were stopped on the street, on the road by one of Celo's soldiers. He asked us where we were going. We told him that we were going to go and pick some tomatoes and peppers. Next to the house where he stopped us, in that house were soldiers and women. He asked us if we wanted to join them, and we refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said "next to the house" are --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, next to the house, the house where he stopped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you tell us, what was -- first tell us: What were the ages of the women that were in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were older women, in their 50s.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing, the women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were crying. They were completely distraught.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember one woman, who was wearing a yellow sweater. She had blond hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are we in open session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We picked the tomatoes and the peppers and returned to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know any soldiers named Hodza or Ferid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you or Tajso visit them that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when did you visit in relation to the incident that you had seen with the women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was there any conversation at that house with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We said what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did you feel at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you stay very long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. We remained there for about a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then after you left Hodza and Ferid's house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to the house where we were sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At this point, without stating the names, if there was anyone there, were there any other soldiers at your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the soldiers from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation with them when you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And please tell the Court about that conversation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the soldiers had already heard and seen what had happened, and we also told them what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did the other soldiers say that they had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they had seen soldiers taking away the local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did the people in the house feel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't easy for anyone, what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did the people in your house have any weapons? The soldiers, I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why didn't the soldiers in your house have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons had been handed in because there were no combat activities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you remained in the house during the evening into the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what you heard or saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, through the remainder of the night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go outside. I went out just the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, as you stayed in the house, could you hear anything during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you hear during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Screaming and shooting, which was probably coming from the victims and the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was coming from the victims and the soldiers, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did you and the other soldiers in the house feel when you heard these yells and screaming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were confused. It wasn't easy for anyone, because we knew what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taking the inhabitants away, killing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have an opinion as to the sobriety of some of those soldiers or some of -- let me step back, sir. Whose soldiers were taking the inhabitants away and doing this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Celo's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you have an opinion as to the sobriety of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not sober.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did you base that on, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the behaviour and because it was known that there were a couple of people in that unit who had a tendency to take alcohol and drugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to the next day. Beginning with the morning, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the house. I walked along the road to see. The place where I saw bodies in the Neretva River, next to the river, I saw a part of a skull and brain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's take it step by step. You got up in the morning. Did you speak to anyone? Starting before you went outside the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you speak to anyone inside the house before you went out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was the discussion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about seeing what had happened. It was very uncomfortable for us. We wanted to return to Sarajevo immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went outside, did you speak with anyone, before you took that walk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. We were all talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any talk outside with people from any other homes, other than the one that you were staying in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to what had occurred during the night in relation to the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was that discussion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said before, we couldn't believe that this had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what had happened that people couldn't -- that the other soldiers couldn't believe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to the extent of the killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there any discussion as to where some of the killings had occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we saw it, yes, we did talk about it, once we saw where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. You went for a walk. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the iron bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you walked towards the iron bridge, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two bodies in the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you describe first the age and sex of those bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were elderly people. I don't know exactly how old they were. It was a man and a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where in the Neretva River were they located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the river bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What else did you see on that walk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the road in the hedges, two more bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us first the sex of those bodies, or the gender of those bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you describe them as best as possible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw one wearing something like a grey suit, a grey jacket. That's what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us about the other person that you saw in the bushes or hedges.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just lying there, the body, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What else did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the iron bridge in a sort of hole, a little bit outside of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say "a hole," do you mean a ravine or do you mean a hole in the ground or do you mean a ditch? What do you mean by "a hole"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like a canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. What did you see in that canyon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two bodies, but I couldn't determine whether they were men or women, because the -- it was quite deep, the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you had seen a piece of a skull or something like that? Could you tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between our houses and the iron bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the soldier or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The woman.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was on the road when we headed out towards the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you please describe how she appeared when you saw her.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she was lying on the road. She was doubled over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was she alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: These bodies that you had seen, were any of them wearing uniforms, military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you saw these dead bodies, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the house, where we slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to any other soldiers before you had returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to any soldiers when you returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had they seen anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What had they seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, the bodies. And each of them told the story as he had experienced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was the mood of the soldiers at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very poor. We simply wanted to leave the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander lined us up because we had asked to leave, to be deployed elsewhere. He said that we should stand guard in front of each house where our soldiers were and to have a bullet ready in the barrel in case we needed to fight with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the commander who lined you up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan Solakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was the ethnic make-up of the -- Adnan Solakovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mixed. There were Serbs and Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did the non-Muslims feel at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was anything done to allay their fears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what happened the previous night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, to -- was anything done to allay -- to reduce their fear or protect any -- the non-Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We changed their names. We didn't call them by their actual names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please explain that, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, if somebody was called Zvonko, we would either call him by a nickname or by a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they feared for their lives and because they were of a different ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, was there any discussion as to how to deal or how to -- or basically what you should deal -- how you should deal with Celo's soldiers? Did Adnan Solakovic give you any orders or advice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us not to mix with them, to avoid them, and as I have already told you, to stand guard in front of our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about Samir Pezo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told us that he had sent a dispatch to Sarajevo with a report on what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you and members of your unit stay very much longer in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: About how much longer did you stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a day or two, and then we went to the tunnel towards Dreznica, where we slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, during that day or two, did you see any high-ranking officers in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say "they came," who came to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Vehbija Karic, Sefer Halilovic, Celo, Zuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's take each one one at a time. Had you ever seen Sefer Halilovic previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where had you seen him previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: On television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen Vehbija Karic previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where? And where had you seen him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen Zuka previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bjelasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And had you ever seen Celo previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion among the soldiers when Halilovic, Karic, Zuka, and Celo came to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did any other soldiers say anything about their visit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. Your Honours, the witness just gave a clear answer to the last question, and this is a -- simply a second try to get an answer, so I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The witness answered that "I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did any other soldiers recognise them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, given the answer to the previous question, that would simply be a third attempt at the same thing; although, disguised in a different way. So I object to it, once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this question is a little bit different with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree with you. It is phrased differently. But the source of knowledge would appear -- this witness can't look into people's minds. He can only have one source of knowledge, and that is what he was told as to whether other people recognised or not. And since he's already given his clear answer as to that source of knowledge, I do keep the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that, you know, the question is that whether somebody told him that he knew those persons or not, the main, you know, thrust of this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what I took it to be as well, Your Honour. And bearing in mind the -- the answer that he gave at I think about line 7, which has now gone off the page, as usual, that's why I've made the objection that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, one question concerns a conversation as to what they could have said, what they could have done. Another one concerns as to whether or not anyone else recognised them. It's a separate and distinguished question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this is totally hearsay evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, as you know, hearsay is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So -- so you -- you had better make it more clear to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did any soldiers state that they recognised any of those four superior officers that came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they saw -- that they saw the command gathering together after what we call roughhousing, after all the fuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "the fuss"? Or "roughhousing"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just -- which events? Could you be more specific.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The killings that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you eventually sent to battle, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the tunnel, where we slept for two nights. After that, we went to the Medved mount.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long were you at the Medved mount.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you returned to Grabovica after that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we returned, but I don't remember where we returned to because the buses were waiting for us there to take us to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, did you stay any other nights in the village of Grabovica after the three days of fighting on the mount?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, but some other people remained there, people from our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now can we move back into private session again, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit P78. And may we have private session just for this one paragraph, please. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you going to use the next document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: P9, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at that photograph. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the road and the iron bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that Grabovica, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The areas where you saw those six dead bodies, can you see them, those areas, in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us or circle the area where you saw the two bodies in the canyon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the areas where you saw the two bodies on the water bank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did you see the bodies in the bushes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I circled just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, okay. I'm sorry. So the -- let's see, 1 is the canyon -- could you put a "1" over the canyon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And put a "2" by the bodies in the bushes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the bodies that were in the water or at the water's edge, where were those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a "3" over that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is the place depicted where you saw the blond woman lying dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we offer that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So it is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Finally, can the witness be shown - and he doesn't have to mark on write on this - Exhibit -- actually, it's 65 ter number 105. In the B/C/S, it's pages 01057858 through 01057936. In the English, 01057892 through 01057895. That's not it. It's a diary. 01057892.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that page, or that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the registrar please scroll to page 7892 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when did you maintain this diary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you discuss the portion or do you -- do you discuss the incident in Grabovica in the diary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in that portion of the diary, do you mention Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you mention Adnan Solakovic on those --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you mention him in those few pages in relation to Grabovica? If you could look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you mention Zuka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is everything that occurred in Grabovica contained in that diary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And this diary, was it prepared for court proceedings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you prepare it for? Why did you maintain it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have some notes so that with the help of the notes and my recollection I could write a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender that diary at this time, or those three pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, there's no objection, but I can indicate that the whole diary should be tendered. But, however, I'm going to ask some questions about that. I don't object to this being tendered now. If my friend wants to tender it in a partial form, he can, but I indicate I'll tender more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine. The whole diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it necessary to -- to tender the whole diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If -- if it will make Defence happy, that's fine. It's the three pages in -- two pages in relation to Grabovica is sufficient, but if -- for -- if the Court would like the whole diary, we have no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps I can assist, Your Honour. I'm grateful to my learned friend for taking the stance that he does. I must say the happiness of the Defence isn't normally the touchstone of admissibility. There's a number of pages that I want to -- want to refer to. It may be after I finish that it's not necessary for the whole diary to be tendered, but I don't want to be picking and choosing either, so perhaps it -- if my friend is permitted to just tender what he wants to tender now, and I indicate I'll be going to other parts of it in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I think the three pages mentioned by Prosecution are admitted into the evidence, and later on we might have more parts to be admitted. But frankly speaking, I don't think it's necessary to admit the whole diary because the diary is a personal record which might involve some privacy of this witness. So we'll only admit the relevant parts to this case. It is so decided. Maybe and later on we could have a number for the whole diary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be 248.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there was no number announced for the last photograph, the second photograph, so 247?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The second photograph is 247.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, has anyone in the military or in the police ever questioned you concerning what you observed in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our army or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, your army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you returned to Sarajevo, did anyone in the police ever question you concerning what you had seen in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long had you remained in Sarajevo after this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Bradina on the 30th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And up to the 30th of November, did you remain in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then after Bradina, did you return to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I would have to look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But did you remain within the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the last document, the diary, out of an abundance of caution, it should be admitted under seal. Well --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's noted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, maybe we could a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness E. I just have a couple preliminary questions about the afternoon when some soldiers from the 9th Brigade arrived. Is it your recollection that those soldiers arrived at around about lunchtime and that the trouble and shooting began at around evening-time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And the trouble and shooting began on the same day that they arrived but maybe five or so hours later; is that approximately accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In that five or so hours between their arrival and the start of the trouble, you saw no bad behaviour and no aggression from those troops; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you see any refugees in the village that afternoon? By which I mean Muslim refugees from areas such as Stolac, Capljina, and other places held by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In your whole time there, did you meet any Muslim refugees whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't meet any of them. They were accommodated on the other side of the Neretva river bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You didn't meet an older refugee called Zulfo who was staying in the house with Adnan himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you arrived in the the village, you didn't have any weapons with -- on your person but those weapons were stored with the more senior officers from your battalion; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons were handed back, and I don't recall if any of the civilians carried any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But when you reached Grabovica, you've indicated in evidence here that you -- you and your friends were not armed. And I'm just asking you about that. Where were your weapons? Were they in the house with Adnan? Adnan Solakovic, I mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And I'm going to ask you who was in which house in just a moment, but I've got some general questions before I get to that point. In the afternoon -- in the hours after the soldiers arrived, by which I mean the 9th Brigade soldiers that you've referred to, you did not personally see Ramiz Delalic at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, do you agree with me that you didn't see him or are you saying that you did see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Nor did you see any other senior officers that afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Once you first heard the -- the noise of -- of gunshots, you indicated that at first you thought this was just celebrating and effectively silly behaviour; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. By the time you walked out the door with Tajso to go and get some peppers and tomatoes, what did you think was going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't really thinking anything until that soldier stopped us, until he said, "Halt. Who's there?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want you to -- would you just excuse me, please, one moment, Witness E. I just need some advice about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the recently tendered Exhibit 245. This may be, Your Honours, in private session, so this -- this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness E, just accept my apologies for this. It does happen from time to time that there are delays with -- with the technology here, but it's worthwhile in the long run. Very well. Well, when you got to -- sorry. Perhaps I'll ask you another topic: The house that you resided in, was that a double house? In other words, was it two houses stuck together, or was it just a single house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. When you were residing there, were there any Croatian civilians also residing there in -- in any part of that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only the owner of the house came to her garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How old was she?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was an elderly woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you able to communicate with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't communicate with her, but other soldiers did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness E, in the time before the soldiers from the 9th Brigade arrived, the villagers had treated you kindly and politely; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In the beginning, there was a little bit of fear when the soldiers came, but later this disappeared because we established contact with them. We exchanged cigarettes, coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I was going to say to you that you and your soldiers also made an effort to be friendly to the local people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And quite frankly, this was entirely consistent with the aims of the Bosnian war effort to create a multi-ethnic and tolerant Bosnia; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And now I just want to turn to the photograph. Do you have in front of you now a clean photograph with those yellow lines on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. What I'll do is get you to mark the houses once again that you did. So mark with a circle and a number "1" the house that you were in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, shall we go back to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness E. So in that house there, the house number 4, during the time when you were present there, is that where you understood Mr. Okovic to be based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there just that one day, and the following day he went to conduct reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And now, although I'm jumping forward in time a little bit, I want to ask you: What time was it to -- to the best of your knowledge that Okovic left the village of Grabovica to go on reconnaissance the following day? Was it morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it before or after you had walked up to the iron bridge and observed the sad sights that you saw that Okovic left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I return to some questions about that house number 4. In the house where -- that you've mentioned as house number 4, who else was staying there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan Solakovic, Samir Pezo, and the limited circle around the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Apart from that particular house, you indicated that there -- to your recollection there might have been a couple of other houses or buildings just nearby but hidden in the trees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it on this picture, but as far as I remember, there was another house there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Having regard to the yellow arrows that you can see, in particular yellow arrows 6, 7, and 8, would you just look -- take a moment now and look at yellow arrows with the numbers 6, 7, and 8, and I'd ask you whether any of those houses --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are any of those arrows pointing to the houses you're talking about or is it just not possible to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not possible to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Apart from the soldiers whose names you've already mentioned, are there any other soldiers from your battalion whose presence you can recall in the village, even if you can't recall exactly what house they were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Firstly, are you able to remember any of their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spiro. I don't remember his last name. Hamo, whose last name I can't remember either; Miroslav Macal; Mujo, whose last name I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And -- okay. Thank you. Very well. I now return to the narrative of -- of what happened. When you walked out with your friend Tajso, you passed by the house that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'd ask that the witness be shown P4, which I believe to be a photograph much tendered in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The photograph I'm seeking to show you now, Witness E, is a -- a more close-up photograph of the area where you were.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P4 is not a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Pardon me. My note is wrong. Would Your Honours just excuse me, please, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We'll make an inquiry and we'll come back to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. Well, when you got up to the -- up to the house of Ferid, could you please indicate there whether there was any communications equipment present in Ferid's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was the battalion's -- not the whole battalion but the part of the battalion in Grabovica. Where was the communications equipment for your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see standing in a threatening way, one of them undressed, near to these women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we might want to go into private session at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But now we have the picture there. Are you going to come to that picture or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we are. We are. We have the -- we have the picture. Sorry. I didn't realise we had it. Thank you. It's possible now that this would involve questions that touch on the private session, so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. How many soldiers were there up at Ferid's house when you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: How many soldiers there were in the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. I remember Hodza and Ferid were there. I think Enver Kapo was there too in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And approximately -- without remembering all the names, approximately how many were there? Do you recall four or five or twelve or twenty? Approximately what number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. When you came to leave that house -- sorry, perhaps I'll -- one more question: You told those three what you had seen, I take it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we came back to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. So -- but my question was: Did you tell the three people at Ferid's house about what you'd seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you then leave Ferid's house and go back to your own house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right away. We were about two or three hours up there, and then we returned to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And when you returned to your house, did you tell the people at your house what you'd seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at that stage, no restrictions had been placed on your movement within the village; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no. But none of the people were moving around anyway because of their own safety concerns. I think that the majority knew what was already starting to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I mean, I think it's fair to say you'd go a bit further because you actually told them what you'd seen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it's quite normal to say what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly. And you had walked back in safe -- in safety from Ferid's house back to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did any of you soldiers who were in your house then set off and walk down to the house where the commanders were, which you've marked as house number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When did you first see one of those commanders? Was it that night or was it the following morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't one of you walk down and tell the commanders, "Look, there's a possible rape going on in that house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The next morning when you walked out, you've indicated that you went to go and look at -- you walked down as far as the iron bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why did you go to the iron bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was already talk that you could see a part of a skull, a brain, that there were bodies lying around. That's why I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And on your way there, were you molested or stopped or spoken to by any soldiers from Ramiz Delalic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers from Ramiz Delalic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On your way to that iron bridge, did you stop at house number 4, where the commanders of the Solakovic units were, and speak to them about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were already a couple of soldiers there and it was already known. There was talk about it. There were those soldiers who were asking that we return to Sarajevo immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What time was it that you woke -- approximately what time was it that you woke up that morning? This being the morning after you saw the women being oppressed in that house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when, but it was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Was it light or just getting light?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already light.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And when you set off to walk to the iron bridge, did you see any checkpoints that had been set up by any military units, either by the 2nd Independent Battalion or by other soldiers that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was a checkpoint, but I don't remember where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I just want you to have a think about that. Was it a checkpoint on the village road near to Adnan Solakovic's house, or was it a checkpoint quite near to your house on the road up which you walked the previous night to visit Ferid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And who was manning that checkpoint? Was it soldiers of the 2nd Independent Battalion or soldiers from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Going back to the previous night for a moment. When you all gathered in the house after you'd seen what you'd seen and after you returned from Ferid, did any of you go down to Adnan Solakovic's house and collect some weapons to defend yourselves or the women with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if anybody went to get weapons, but perhaps they went to go to report what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry to say that perhaps is not really the -- the answer I'm looking for. Do you recall whether or not they did go to report that or do you adhere to your earlier answers on that topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes, but I -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were friends -- one thing about the 2nd Battalion was that it was not a racially prejudiced unit and you had a lot of different ethnic backgrounds in that unit; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to ask him about a couple of those friends, and it may be appropriate to go to the private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, I was asking you some questions about your movements the following day, and you indicated that you attended at the end of the village and observed the sad sight of some killed people there. Could I just ask you about -- about what you were able to see at that point. First of all, when you -- I want to ask you about the -- the people that you saw in the ravine. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- by "the ravine," do you mean a cutting in the hill which passed underneath that iron bridge with water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the persons that you saw on that occasion, were they in the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's the only time you saw those two people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You also saw two people in bushes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you've already described those. I won't make you describe them again. But that's the only time you saw those two people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And finally, you saw two persons in the water on the edge of the river; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And once again, that's the only time you saw those two persons; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And could I just ask you: Approximately what time of the morning was it that you saw these people? I understand you can't be precise, but be as precise as you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, until about 9.30 in the morning. 9.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want to work from that time and ask you what your movements were for the rest of that morning. After you saw that sad sight, did you then walk back to your own house, or did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. While you were returning to the house, did you notice any refugees in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you hear any screams in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you hear screams and shooting throughout the previous night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But by the time you came to the -- to the iron bridge, those -- those screams and that shooting had finished; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. There was no more shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And from your memory, at all times at which there was shooting you were always inside your house; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And while you were walking back from the iron bridge, did you notice any soldiers wearing masks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to any soldiers from the Handzar Division or see any such soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you encounter any soldiers from the unit sometimes called Cedo's Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you encounter a unit describing itself as the Tigrovi, the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in short and in summary, you didn't encounter any soldiers on that walk of yours except for soldiers from the 2nd Independent Battalion; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Is it correct to say that by 10.00 or approximately 10.00 of that morning you were back at your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At approximately what time did you speak to any of the commanders concerning your safety and the need for you to have weapons and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately upon our return, we were ordered to line up, and that's when Adnan ordered us to keep guard in front of the houses and to give other names and nicknames to these people and not to mix with the rest of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The line-up to which you've referred --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be given the opportunity to look at photograph P7. The photograph on the screen, I believe, is P7. That's the photograph I want. I just want to be sure that it is P7. But that is the photograph that I want, in any event. And it's labeled 01494612. Well, could the witness please be given the opportunity now to mark with a pen where that line-up was, if in fact it took place on this -- And, Your Honours, I don't know if this is a matter where we have to go back to the private session or not. I don't believe we do, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do we have to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't see any reason at this point to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm happy not to. That's good. I'm sorry. I thought I misunderstood something I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Does that photograph show where the line-up took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did the line-up take place near to house number 4, the Solakovic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I would ask, then, that the witness be shown photograph P3, the panoramic photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you have a panoramic photograph in front of you now. I just want you to mark two things on this photograph. With a "1", I want you to mark where the checkpoint was. Just draw a line or a -- or a mark where the checkpoint was. And then with a "2", I'll get you to mark where the line-up took place that -- that the commanders got you to do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember where the command ramp was, but we lined up there on the road. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And approximately how many of you were there lining up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all there. I don't remember the exact number of soldiers there though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was -- were arms issued to you at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I tender that -- I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is 252, and the previous document, before mentioned, is 251.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after you were issued -- and am I right to -- to conclude that that line-up took place at approximately 10.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And during that time, you didn't hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you didn't happen to see a certain Croatian villager aged in his 20s fleeing from the village at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Or any people fleeing from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Or any Bosniak Muslim refugees in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And after that meeting, did you go back to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you play your part in standing guard outside that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And where did the Serbian and Croat members of your household go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were with us. They didn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall whether an order came along for the Serbian or Croatian members of your unit to go and stay in another house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you didn't see any trucks coming to collect bodies that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you weren't aware of any persons burying bodies that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you didn't see two small boys being escorted by members of Ramiz Delalic's unit anywhere in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you didn't know -- you didn't see any livestock being moved by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you approached by any members of any other unit with fresh cow meat to be used or eaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see anyone bringing such meat to your household?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, yes, there was meat, but I don't remember who brought it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where were you when it was brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the house, but I don't know who brought it. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, in the discussions that took place in your household, what was the news about where that meat came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Can you recall what time your commander, Adnan Solakovic, arrived in the village on that day, if it was on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was he there at any time the previous night, or did he arrive on the morning after you saw the women being oppressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember when he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When did you first see him yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And was that when your -- when -- did that take place when your -- when you men were lined up outside the command house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was it after that that Mr. Okovic went off on reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who did he go with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is, again, something that was up to the command. Us soldiers didn't know who went with whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see him leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you were inside that house of yours after the line-up and after you got weapons, what sort of a view did you have of the village? Did you have a good view from windows or from a balcony, or did you have a very narrow view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a view from our balcony on the River Neretva and the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you spend your time on the balcony, or given the security situation, did you remain inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now, you've given an account that sometime later you saw some senior officers, and you named Vehbija Karic, Sefer Halilovic, Zuka, and Celo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask -- I want to ask you: Where were you when you saw that -- saw those individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they passed by in the jeep, I was on the balcony. They went off in the direction of the tunnel, towards Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it an open jeep -- an open-top jeep or was it a closed-top jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: A jeep with a roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was driving that jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What speed was the jeep going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was going slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did the people in the jeep stop and get out and talk to people in your building, or did they just proceed going in the direction they were going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were talking to somebody. I don't know with whom though. And then they just passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. For how long did you see that -- that jeep stopped still? Was it a matter of just a few seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see the jeep when it was standing. I just saw it passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. So you didn't see the people from the jeep talking to other people. You just saw the jeep moving along. Is that an accurate comment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to the command, talked there, and then later each of us soldiers who saw something there also -- probably some of the soldiers saw something there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I don't mean to mislead you or trick you in any way here, Witness E. I just got to ask you about what you saw with your own eyes, if that's okay. Now, what you've indicated that what you saw with your own eyes was seen from the house that you stayed in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the terrace, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And you yourself did not see the jeep when it was stopped outside the command post; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But you came out to the terrace and you saw the jeep going past; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. So at that time you got a chance to see the people who were on your side of the car; is that an accurate way to put it? As it drove past?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And when you looked at those people there, you saw men in military uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One of them with black hair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you yourself and -- and sorry, and perhaps I should ask you this: How long did you have that moving vehicle in view? Did you have it in view for five second or ten seconds or -- or a longer period than that? Would you please tell the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And you'd never seen Sefer Halilovic -- well, sorry, I take that back. You had seen Halilovic on television before, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: And personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But you concede this, don't you, Witness E: That it's possible that although you thought you saw Sefer Halilovic, the person you saw was actually someone else? Do you agree with that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As to the form of the question. This one he's asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- I think this question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. But I don't want there to be any -- any speculation. I'll rephrase it. I'll deal with it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
