utterances.text: You had a short time -- just tell me if you agree or disagree with these propositions. You had a short time to see this man; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I recognised the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand you say that, but just deal with the propositions I'm putting to you. You had a short time to see him. Secondly, he was in a moving vehicle; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And thirdly, you say you've recognised four people, don't you? Zuka, Celo, Karic, and Halilovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were those -- where were those four sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you again: Do you concede the possibility that you've made an honest mistake, that you saw someone that you think was Halilovic but that it's possible that you personally have made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Halilovic sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks. Back or front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Front.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How many people were sitting in the front seat? Two or three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two. The driver and the person next to the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was sitting in the back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vehbija Karic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about Celo? What about Zuka? Where were they sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in the car. They were outside, next to the command headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How could you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: After their departure with the jeep, they remained in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you approach them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see them. When we came out, we saw them walking on the road and talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness E, you knew when you returned -- well, I'll come to that in a minute. You knew when you returned from your fighting duties down at Dreznica, when you got back to Sarajevo, that there was likely to be an investigation into what happened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you knew that your -- your superiors in the 2nd Independent Battalion had passed on a report to the 1st Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you knew that you yourself, of course, had nothing to do with the killings or the coverings-up or any of the other bad behaviour; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you also knew that when a bad incident like this takes place, blame can be spread around quite wrongly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: If nothing was done, then how could we be blamed for it? We couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not suggesting that you did do anything wrong. But do you agree with this: Sometimes people do try to shift the blame onto other people. In your experience, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about your diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's the right time for us to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you are changing the subject to this diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the diary is ready in the e-court system. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness E. Just before we get to the diary though, there's one last series of questions I have for you concerning your view of this jeep and so on. Now, you made a statement sometime ago now, on the 7th of October, 2000, to a man named Nikolai Mikhailov with an interpreter present called Marc Jeffery, and on that occasion you said this: "During the war, I wrote my original notes immediately or sometime soon after the events while they were still fresh in my mind in a small diary and on various pieces of paper. I rewrote these into a black desk diary in 1995." Now, first of all, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you told that to Nikolai Mikhailov, the investigator, you were determined to tell the truth about that diary; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what you say is that's what you told him, that's what he wrote down, and that's why you were prepared to sign that statement to that effect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And indeed, Witness E, we don't -- or the -- the Tribunal doesn't have the original of that diary before them, but you've got it in your hand -- or you've got it before you there, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the diary itself is a 1995 diary; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And so that when you told -- so that when you told Nikolai Mikhailov about that, he recorded what you said perfectly accurately in that statement, and that's why you signed the statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In that statement, on page 5, you said this: "I saw Sefer Halilovic and Vehbija Karic, Zuka, some other senior military commanders, Ramiz Delalic, Celo, Caco, and Adnan Solakovic walk along the village road towards the exit from the village in the direction of the tunnel in the direction of Dreznica." Was that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, today you have said that you saw Sefer Halilovic being driven in a jeep. Which one is true?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. That's a mischaracterisation of the evidence. He has Sefer Halilovic in a jeep. He has Sefer Halilovic down -- down the road with the -- by Adnan Solakovic's house. And then there's this. That's a mischaracterisation of the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe if witness could explain to us. Witness, would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After what happened, everybody assembled in the village from the command. I don't know what they talked about. Adnan didn't say -- or Adnan didn't convey to us what they talked about. My statement can be confirmed also by a number of soldiers who also saw what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But the question is - and it's been put to you very clearly - in your statement you said, "I saw Sefer Halilovic," you then list a number of others -- I'll read you the whole thing. But you say: "I say Sefer Halilovic, and Vehbija Karic, Zuka, some other senior military commanders, Ramiz Delalic, Celo, Caco, and Adnan Solakovic walk along the village road ..." Now, the question is: Since today you say you saw Halilovic in a jeep, which one's true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you now wish to amend your evidence to say that you also saw Mr. Halilovic walk down the road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, I believe that you could give a chance to this witness for him to explain why there's two contradictory evidence here. Maybe the witness saw your client twice or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree that the witness should be given precisely that opportunity, and that's really what the question was designed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So -- so, Witness E, what do you wish to assert now; that you saw him more than once on that day or do you have some other explanation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him more than once that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Why did you not say that you'd seen him more than once when you were asked questions by the Prosecutor and when you were asked questions by me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forgot. I was a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I now have some questions to ask you about your diary. Have you told the truth about writing your diary in 1995 before this Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I ask that the witness please be shown a particular page of the diary. I'll have to give the particular ERN number of that page. It's 01057890.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have that page in front of you -- I'm sorry, Witness E, just wait for a moment, please. I apologise for this. When you have -- when it's in front of you -- I'll ask you the question. Would it be possible that the page be scrolled down to see the bottom few lines of that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not have an English translation of this segment, but it's not the substance so much as something else, which we'll come to in a moment. And what I have in mind is to ask the witness to read live into the transcript this section and something over the page and then I'll ask for his comment, and I hope that it will be more than satisfactory when that's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but as a rule, Mr. Morrissey, if you're using a piece of the evidence, you have the obligation to have it translated into the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's so, Your Honour. And frankly, I apologise for it. It's really a matter that's -- it has little to do with the translation. I acknowledge what Your Honour says. We probably should have. And I -- I apologise for that. What I'd seek leave of the Court to do is to press on, ask the witness to read that in. If there is any disadvantage to the Prosecutor, of course we won't resist any remedy at all. But it will be apparent while I'm doing it when it's -- when it's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll see how far we could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you have, Witness E, in front of you the page which begins with "The 13th of February -- Monday, the 13th of February," at least in the -- in the official notations in the top left-hand corner. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could the witness now please be shown down to the bottom of the page again. And I'd ask you to read, please, the last six lines of that page and the first line on the following page. So could you please just read that out loud and the interpreters will translate it as we go.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: "What exactly happened, I don't know, because I wasn't present, but I know for a fact that many stories have circulated to this day. But the truth is that he's gone and" -- and then the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we please have the top of the next page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. It will take a moment, Witness E, for that to be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the next page will be 01057891.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To this day, 26 of April, 1998, nothing is known about him, whether he is alive or dead."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The truth is you wrote this in 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in 1998, you were under pressure from the police because you had recently been charged with offences; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you were very worried that -- and also, you knew that there was an investigation into the crimes at Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And at that time, in 1998, you wrote out this diary, I suggest to you, as a way of protecting yourself against wrongful accusations that you had something to do with these crimes. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that the reason you didn't mention Sefer Halilovic's presence in the village is because you didn't see Sefer Halilovic present in the village at any time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you also agree that at the time when these events happened in September of 1993, you had some problems with marijuana use? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps before the witness answers that, I'm not sure what protections witnesses ought to be furnished with, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as a principle, I believe all the hearings should be conducted in the open session unless one of the parties made a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you making that request, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not making it, Your Honour, but I just thought I'd give fair warning because --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I am. And I want to know how this is relevant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's relevant as to the credibility of this witness, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we -- shall we into the private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: After your -- sorry, pardon me. I'll go back to that question again. Some days after the killings in Grabovica, your unit went off to fight at Dreznica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In your diary, you have not recorded the precise number of nights that you spent at Grabovica; is that correct too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you, I suggest -- well, according to you, the day when you say that you saw these commanders, that was on either the last or the second-last day of your stay in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The penultimate day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The second-last day. Just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness E, thank you for your patience in answering the questions. That's the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just -- just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement to the OTP, you said the following - and this relates to the diary - "During the war, I wrote my original notes immediately or sometime soon after the events while they were still fresh in my mind in a small diary and on various pieces of paper. I rewrote these in a black desk diary in 1995. The first page of the diary says '1995, Termin Tagebuch, personlisches'". Sir, could you please explain what you did, when you wrote the diary, when -- was it 1995, 1998. Please just tell the Court what you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I started writing it in 1995, and I copied the text from the papers, from the loose papers, whenever I had time. When I finished that, you can translate what is stated on the last page, the 28th of September, which was a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when did you complete the information in that diary, complete drafting it or writing it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when I finished that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The information in that diary, where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personal knowledge and what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, the information contained in that diary, is it true to the best of your knowledge, information, and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The particular abstract concerning Grabovica, does that describe in part what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, only partially, without details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you were questioned by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2000, did you add additional details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are those true?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, hang on. Sorry. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me. Sorry. That -- I withdraw the objection. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, counsel asked you about a specific extract which you wrote in 1998. First, where and when did you write that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to this. There may be some matters of clarification that are necessary, but it has to be remembered that evidence about this diary was led in evidence in chief and presumably following proofing. Now, the Prosecutor led what he chose to lead at that time about the diary as being relevant to these proceedings. Having been cross-examined now, in my submission, it's not appropriate to start on a whole -- start at the beginning again with that diary, that -- the evidence was led by my friend as it was. Now, this appears to be an attempt to re-commence evidence in chief. And so I object to it. However, I note of course if there are matters of clarification, then they are naturally legitimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that extract written in 1998 was

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: or to make some clarification on that issue. Yes, Mr. Weiner, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us where and when did you draft that extract?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wrote it at home when I had time, as I've just told you, because after the war my memory was still fresh. All of these events were still fresh in my memory and I wasn't able to write it down immediately. I wanted to forget, but I was unable to. And I wanted to use these notes to write something later, to write in more detail about each operation and each area that we were deployed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm afraid you did not answer the question put to you by the Prosecutor, because he specifically asked about that extract, where and when did you write those extracts.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: Let's take it one step at a time. First, where did you write it, that particular extract, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: And do you know approximately when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the date is there.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: And could you tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey, do you want to help?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't want to intervene. I can hold it up if it helps all in court to know what page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, on the 26th of April, 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: And did you continue to write and complete that diary after that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: And could you tell us again, what's the reason that you were writing this diary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason I wrote the diary is that I wanted to use my notes in order to describe each operation and each area from the beginning to the end and to mention all of my pals from the 2nd Independent.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: And what did you plan to do with this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that, to write it down. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE DEFENCE TEAM
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you -- did you ever provide any information to that diary or did you ever write any information in that diary while you were under the influence of alcohol or anything else, any other substance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Judges? Judge El Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. I would like to seek some clarification. Could you give us some dates. You said that when you arrived in Grabovica some days later some troops had arrived. Do you remember when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But you do confirm that it is on the night of their arrival that the events unfolded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you stated that on the next morning after the events you were home or in the house and around 10.00 in the morning you saw the jeep in which Mr. Halilovic was, according to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean that I saw that in the morning. They lined us up in the morning; our command did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At what time did you see the jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is still on the day after the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the morning, there was this line-up outside the command house, and then you returned to the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you said that you saw the jeep when you were on the balcony or on the terrace.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this on the first floor or on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was the jeep going or where was it coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the direction of our command, moving towards Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the driver was on your side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You saw Mr. Halilovic a second time. When was it? After you saw him in the jeep? Was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before. Before he passed in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, where were you, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house, on the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which road? And what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. We were just standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doing what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Like I said, we were just standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So close to the command place or close to the house where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't give any names, but were you alone or were together with somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: With somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And were you -- did you have weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But were you on orders of your commander who told you to be positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we weren't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But was it a habit of yours just to walk about being armed in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a habit. It was immediately after the line-up and after the weapons were issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but was that on -- on the basis of orders, or were you complying with orders that had been given? Had you been ordered to be stationed there, there where you were? Was it so or did you decide yourself to be there? Was this by chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Purely by chance. There was no order for us to be there. We were just standing there talking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And thereafter, you returned to the house, did you, or did you just walk around the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long we were on the road. After that, we returned to the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my last question will be as follows: So you mentioned the jeep, and you said it happened in the afternoon. Around what time? Was it still daylight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm quoting you in English: [In English] "I don't remember. Yes." [Interpretation] How am I to understand your question "I don't remember. Yes" -- or your answer, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which question did I say that to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was saying that you said that when you saw Mr. Halilovic in the jeep, it was in the afternoon. And I asked you at what time and whether it was during the daytime, whether there was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was daytime. You could still see. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge El Mahdi. Any questions out of Judge's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one arising directly from that. Could I indicate what it is. I wish to put a passage from the -- a statement which the witness made, of which I've already put part of the statement. But it relates to the -- the timing of the jeep -- the day on which the jeep arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness E. This is at page 4 of the version -- the English version in the final paragraph. In the statement you provided to the OTP, you said this: "One day later" -- sorry, "One day later, that is, the second day after I first saw the dead bodies in the village, I saw Sefer Halilovic and Vehbija Karic, Zuka, and some other senior military commanders in the village." Now, in answer to a question by Judge El Mahdi, you seemed to indicate to the Court that you saw this -- this jeep on the same day as the line-up, and your evidence earlier was that the line-up took place shortly after seeing the bodies. So my question to you is: Did you see, according to you, Sefer Halilovic, Vehbija Karic, and the others on the same day that you saw the bodies and did the line-up, or as you said in your statement, did you see them one day later, that is, "the second day after I first saw the dead bodies in the village"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't answer that question. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, if the fault lies in the question, I'll put it to you clearly so that there's no problem. You've told the investigators clearly in the signed statement that you didn't see Sefer Halilovic, Vehbija Karic, and the others until one day later, that is, the second day after you first saw the dead bodies in the village. That's what you told the investigators. Now in your answer to Judge El Mahdi's questions you seem to suggest that you Sefer Halilovic, Vehbija Karic, and the others on the same day that you saw the bodies. And my question is: Which one is right? Which day did you see these -- the -- the commanders that you claim you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day after what happened in the village, the day after. So it's the next day. The first day when we came; and then the next day is the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. In those circumstances, why did you say to Judge El Mahdi that you had the weapons and you were standing out on the road because it was immediately after the line-up in front of the command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean why did I say it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why did you say to Judge El Mahdi -- just excuse me. I'll find the exact passage. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At page 87, Your Honours, line 3, Judge El Mahdi asked a question. Witness E, I'll put the question and I'll put the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI ASKED
utterances.text: "Was it a habit of yours just to walk around -- walk about being armed in the village?" And you answered: "No, it wasn't a habit. It was immediately after the line-up and after the weapons were issued."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, why did you give that answer, if it now is your evidence that you didn't see Halilovic and Karic and the others until the following day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand. The first day when we arrived, and then the next day, that's the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What is -- what is your position? I'm sorry, I -- I'm misunderstanding you now. In the hope of clarifying, I'm not sure I have. So let me be clear about this. Are you suggesting -- when you said to Judge El Mahdi that you had those weapons and you were standing around immediately after the line-up, was it your position at that point that Sefer Halilovic, Karic, Zuka, and so on had been on the -- in the village on the very same day that you saw these bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in the village the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender? I guess none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think we've tendered everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. I apologise to you for having kept you here for so long. When Madam Usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do we have the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll be taking the next witness. The Prosecution has a -- an application for protective measures in relation to that witness. I informed Defence counsel and the registry before. Is it an appropriate time to make the application now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- perhaps we should go into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.
